title: Junta Jet Kills 16-Year-Old Girl, Injures 8 in Four Bombing Runs on Samee Town
detail: Between 11:23pm and 11:40pm on August 12, 2026, a junta fighter jet carried out four consecutive bombing runs on Ward 2 of Samee Town, Paletwa Township, Chin State, an AA-controlled area on the upper Kaladan River. A 16-year-old girl was killed and 8 residents were injured, including three children aged 8, 10, and 11. The strike came a day after a separate junta bomb injured two teenage girls near the entrance to Paletwa Town, part of an intensifying aerial campaign across AA/CNF-contested townships along the Rakhine-Chin border.

media.caption: Junta jet bombs Samee Town, Paletwa Township, killing a 16-year-old girl and injuring 8 in four bombing runs.

title: Resistance Forces Ambush Junta Column on Thayet-Mindon Road, Magway Region
detail: On August 12, 2026, resistance forces attacked a junta military column of roughly 35 troops near Puzinda village on the Thayet-Mindon road in Magway Region. The clash lasted about 30 minutes; resistance sources claimed nine junta soldiers were killed before the column withdrew to nearby villages, raising local concern about retaliatory airstrikes and artillery fire.

media.caption: Resistance forces ambush a junta column near Puzinda village on the Thayet-Mindon road, Magway Region.

title: Flooding Kills 25, Displaces 220,000+ Across Sagaing, Magway, Mandalay and Ayeyarwady
detail: Torrential monsoon rain and dam discharges from the Thaphanseik and Kabo dams triggered severe flooding across Sagaing, Magway, Mandalay and Ayeyarwady regions in the days leading up to August 12, 2026. At least 25 people were killed and 2 remained missing across 13-17 townships; roughly 220,000 residents were displaced and more than 440,000 people affected nationwide. Sagaing Region — where Khin-U, Kanbalu, Kyunhla, Taze, Shwebo, Kawlin and Depayin townships were hardest hit — accounted for over half the affected population. Residents told DVB that despite regime claims of relief funding, 'nobody in the community has received any relief assistance or supplies.'

media.caption: Severe flooding displaces over 220,000 people across Sagaing, Magway, Mandalay and Ayeyarwady regions.

title: Junta Troops Shut Down Sagaing Bridge, Confiscate Medicine Bound for Flood Victims
detail: Amid the deadly Sagaing flooding, junta troops shut down the Sagaing (Yadanabon) Bridge — the main crossing linking Sagaing and Mandalay — on August 12, 2026, turning back all vehicles carrying relief supplies from Mandalay and Yangon. Military checkpoints along roads into Sagaing confiscated medical supplies and blocked aid convoys; a volunteer aid worker told DVB that 'aid workers fear for their security, so many cannot reach Sagaing to deliver supplies.' The Myanmar Air Force separately conducted three airstrikes on flood-hit Khin-U Township the same day with no reported casualties, plus reconnaissance flights over Wetlet, Shwebo and Sagaing towns.

media.caption: Junta troops shut down the Sagaing Bridge and confiscate medicine bound for flood victims.
